skill.name: motion-graphics
skill.description: Creates short, unnarrated motion graphics with HyperFrames, including kinetic text, charts, logo reveals, overlays, maps, article highlights, webpage demos, and asset-fusion shots.
skill.summary: Plan, build, render, and verify short motion graphics from text, data, brands, webpages, news, maps, or images.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, CSS terms, and fixed argument-array process calls. Confirmed risks include silent remote updates, unsandboxed remote browser code, unrestricted tile endpoints, external image upload with query-string credentials, predictable temporary storage, and disclosed network dependencies.

remediation.issue: The skill silently updates itself and may mutate the global skill set.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update instruction. Require explicit approval, pin the source revision, show planned changes, and verify downloaded artifacts before installation.

remediation.issue: The map baker executes remote CDN scripts in Chrome with sandboxing disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle dependencies locally with integrity verification and run Chrome with its sandbox. If CI requires no-sandbox, isolate the process in a restricted container.

remediation.issue: The map style accepts arbitrary tile URL templates.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist HTTPS tile hosts and reject loopback, link-local, private-network, file, data, and other non-approved destinations before launching the browser.

remediation.issue: The automatic locator uploads images and embeds GEMINI_API_KEY in a URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit upload consent, disclose the destination, use an approved credential header, avoid URL secrets, and provide a local-only default.

remediation.issue: The locator uses a predictable shared temporary font path.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private directory with mkdtemp, use restrictive permissions, avoid check-then-copy logic, and remove temporary files after processing.

content.user_title: Create Short Motion Graphics with HyperFrames
content.value_statement: Short motion graphics require coordinated planning, assets, animation, rendering, and quality checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a reusable HyperFrames workflow.
actual_capabilities: Plans short motion graphics with a structured shot plan and category-specific rules.
Builds kinetic typography, statistics, charts, logo reveals, lower thirds, maps, and visual callouts.
Animates captured webpages, news articles, tweets, and image-based data graphics.
Reuses HyperFrames blocks and paused GSAP timelines for deterministic rendering.
Renders MP4, WebM, or MOV outputs and runs lint and inspection checks.
Locates image regions with a two-stage grid workflow or an optional Gemini detector.
limitations: It targets short, unnarrated graphics, usually under ten seconds and no longer than about thirty seconds.
It requires Node.js, FFmpeg, HyperFrames, and a supported Chrome installation for some workflows.
Search, capture, map, and detector features can send requests or source material to external services.
Users must verify source rights, factual accuracy, brand rules, and final visual quality.

use_cases.title: Produce Social Motion Posts
use_cases.description: Turn a quote, statistic, logo, or announcement into a short vertical or square motion graphic.

use_cases.title: Demonstrate Product Interfaces
use_cases.description: Capture a webpage and animate scrolling, cursor movement, highlights, zooms, and callouts without narration.

use_cases.title: Explain Data Visually
use_cases.description: Animate charts, maps, article facts, or image geometry into a focused data story.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Motion Graphic
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-second 9:16 motion graphic for [message]. Use [colors], large readable text, one clear motion motif, and an MP4 output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with supplied text and style

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Statistic
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an eight-second 1:1 statistic animation for [value and context]. Include a count-up, one supporting chart element, and a clear final hold.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Webpage Highlight
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture [URL] and create a seven-second 16:9 highlight. Show [element], animate a cursor interaction, zoom accurately, and add one concise callout.

prompt_templates.title: Fuse an Asset with Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [image] to visualize [data]. Ground the target geometry, derive the palette from the image, connect graphics to the asset, and render a transparent overlay.

output_examples.input: Create a six-second vertical graphic announcing 2 million users with a dark background and bright green accents.
output_examples.output: A six-second vertical MP4 with a count-up, supporting ring animation, restrained labels, and a readable final hold.

output_examples.input: Animate a product pricing page and highlight the annual plan button without narration.
output_examples.output: A short webpage animation with a captured page, controlled scroll, cursor movement, exact button highlight, click ripple, and final zoom.

output_examples.input: Show a map zoom from Europe to France, then draw the French border and add a label.
output_examples.output: A deterministic map video with a baked basemap, camera move, live border overlay, label entrance, and project-local coordinate data.

best_practices: Provide the message, duration, aspect ratio, brand colors, source assets, and required output format.
Use one visual motif and one primary message so the final frame remains readable.
Review sourced assets, grounded positions, lint results, inspection output, and the rendered video before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for narrated, live-action, or complex multi-scene videos.
Do not depend on live network data during rendering because outputs must remain deterministic.
Do not estimate image or webpage coordinates when grounding or DOM measurements are available.

faq.question: What types of motion graphics can this skill create?
faq.answer: It supports kinetic text, statistics, charts, logos, lower thirds, maps, article highlights, webpage demos, tweets, and asset-fusion graphics.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow renders MP4 by default and can use WebM or MOV for transparent overlays.

faq.question: Does it support narration?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for short, unnarrated graphics where motion communicates the message.

faq.question: Can it use external webpages or news articles?
faq.answer: Yes. Search-driven categories can capture or source material, then freeze it into project-local assets before rendering.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: No. API keys are optional, but some generation, search, or automatic image detection features need provider access.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Node.js, FFmpeg, HyperFrames, and a supported Chrome installation are required for the complete workflow.
